subject: Reranker evaluation scope, auth & SDK onboarding — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Eve Chapman <eve.chapman@rankwave.io>, Tom Li <tom.li@rankwave.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Reranker evaluation scope, auth & SDK onboarding — post-demo clarifications

Hi Eve / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Short recap and a few clarifying questions so our engineers can get a prototype up quickly:

1) Acceptance criteria / signals: you mentioned precision@10 and a few manual relevance slices (FAQ responses, product pages). Can you confirm the primary metric (precision@k vs. NDCG) and one example slice we should prioritise?

2) SDK + auth: Are you planning to use our Java SDK (server-side) or the Python SDK from a backend microservice? Also need to confirm whether RankWave will use API keys (hosted) or a mutual-TLS / VPC private deployment for the pilot.

3) Top_k behaviour: you noted you regularly show top 5 results to users with a re-ranking overlay. Do you expect the reranker to operate on top_k=50 retrievals, or keep a smaller candidate set (top_k=20) and rely on embeddings/fuzzy heuristics first? Any constraints on latency (p95 target)?

4) Structured output / tool calling: you hinted at a downstream classifier that reads structured fields (category, intent). Will you need Redwood to provide structured tool-calls (json schema) from the model, or is the reranker output consumed only by your scoring microservice?

Attachments: I uploaded the recording and a short sample CSV with your earlier queries (sample-queries-topk.csv).

Proposed immediate next actions:
- RankWave: confirm metric slice and latency SLO by EOD Friday (Aug 7)
- Redwood eng (Vanessa / Ben): put up a sandbox API key + simple Java/Python SDK bootstrap and a minimal route that accepts a batch of embeddings + candidate ids
- Sergio: prepare draft eval plan and test harness (will share link)

Short call if helpful — 30 minutes tomorrow or Thursday?

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 20:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Reranker evaluation scope, auth & SDK onboarding — post-demo clarifications

Thanks Sergio — great recap. Quick answers inline.

> 1) Acceptance criteria / signals
We want to optimize for precision@5 for the initial pilot (we surface 5 items in the UI). NDCG is interesting but for business approval we need a clear improvement in precision@5 over current BM25-baseline on the product page slice (we'll send a labelled subset of 1,200 examples).

> 2) SDK + auth
We'll run a Python backend (Flask) that calls Redwood. For the pilot we'll use API keys (hosted) but must ensure token rotation and scoped keys per environment. If the pilot meets perf targets, we'll evaluate a VPC/private deployment later.

> 3) Top_k behaviour
We generally retrieve top_k=100 from the retriever but would like the reranker to re-score top_k=50 to balance compute and recall. Latency target: interactive product detail pages — p95 end-to-end under 250ms (including network + rerank). If that's tough for 50 candidates, we can look at 20 as a fallback.

> 4) Structured output / tool calling
For now, reranker output will feed our scoring microservice (no structured tool-calls required). However, we will want the model to emit an optional JSON blob with a confidence score and taxonomy tag when available. That would help downstream heuristics.

We'll upload the labelled slice (product-pages_1200.csv) by EOD tomorrow.

Happy to take the 30m slot on Thursday 10:00 PDT if that works — Tom and I can join.

Cheers,
Eve
Eve Chapman
Head of Search, RankWave
Eve.Chapman@rankwave.io

Subject: Re: Reranker evaluation scope, auth & SDK onboarding — post-demo clarifications

Thanks Eve — that's helpful. A few follow ups and an internal task split so we can move fast: 

- Metric / dataset: RankWave to share product-pages_1200.csv and a short doc describing the evaluation script format (CSV columns + label conventions). Once we have those, Redwood will run a baseline BM25 + our default reranker on the slice and surface precision@5 and p95 latency numbers.

- Auth & keys: Vanessa, can you provision a sandbox API key with scoped read-only rerank access (expiry 30 days) and a key-rotation policy note? Also include an example of how to create a scoped key via the Console and via the API. Ben — please include Python SDK snippet showing token refresh flow.

- Top_k tuning: Ben, can you prototype two runs: reranker(top_k=50) and reranker(top_k=20) and capture p95 latency and precision@5? We'll put the candidate generation cost on RankWave's retriever (they'll send embeddings + ids), and Redwood will accept a batch POST with JSON that includes candidate ids, embeddings optional, and a config block (top_k, return_structured).

- Structured output: We'll support an optional return_structured=true flag that returns a small JSON blob schema {taxonomy:string, confidence:float}. We'll provide the schema in the proposal PDF.

I'll schedule Thurs 10:00 PDT and add a 15-minute engineering sync before the demo run.

Sergio

Quick update from the eng side after a first pass:

1) Sandbox key: Vanessa has created a scoped sandbox key RW-SANDBOX-85 (expiry 2026-09-04). Console link: https://console.redwood.com/sandbox-keys/RW-SANDBOX-85 (I'll paste the step-by-step in the Drive note). Key provides rerank:read and eval:ingest scope only.

2) SDK snippets: Attached is a minimal Python snippet (we'll add to the Drive link) that demonstrates: chunked POST, token refresh, and optional return_structured flag. Example: POST /v1/rerank with body: {"candidates": [{"id":"doc_1","embedding": [...]}, ...], "config": {"top_k":50, "return_structured":true}}

3) Latency run plan: I'll run the two candidate sizes (20 / 50) against a 1k-sample subset once RankWave uploads the labelled 1,200. Expected p95 for top_k=50 on our dedicated medium pool ~ 170-230ms; for top_k=20 ~ 110-150ms. Will confirm numbers after the runs and include CPU/GPU usage profile.

4) Outputs: We'll return a per-candidate score + optional structured blob (taxonomy, confidence). The structured blob will be very small (under 150 bytes) and backward compatible if you skip return_structured.

Action items assigned:
- RankWave: upload product-pages_1200.csv and confirm sample query format (Eve/Tom)
- Vanessa: share sandbox Console steps + rotation note
- Ben: run latency / precision@5 experiments and drop results in Drive; I'll tag the HubSpot deal RW-2026-9 with the experiment artifacts

I'll join the Thursday 10:00 PDT sync.
